kurals.tr: Patratra Kannum Pazhaimaipaa Raattudhal / Sutraththaar Kanne Ula
kurals.m: Even when (a man's) property is all gone, relatives will act towards him with their accustomed (kindness)

kurals.tr: Virupparaach Chutram Iyaiyin Arupparaa / Aakkam Palavum Tharum
kurals.m: If (a man's) relatives remain attached to him with unchanging love, it will be a source of everincreasing wealth

kurals.tr: Alavalaa Villaadhaan Vaazhkkai Kulavalaak / Kotindri Neernirain Thatru
kurals.m: The wealth of one who does not mingle freely with his relatives, will be like the filling of water in a

kurals.tr: Sutraththaal Sutrap Pataozhukal Selvandhaan / Petraththaal Petra Payan
kurals.m: To live surrounded by relatives, is the advantage to be derived from the acquisition of wealth

kurals.tr: Kotuththalum Insolum Aatrin Atukkiya / Sutraththaal Sutrap Patum
kurals.m: He will be surrounded by numerous relatives who manifests generosity and affability

kurals.tr: Perungotaiyaan Penaan Vekuli Avanin / Marungutaiyaar Maanilaththu Il
kurals.m: No one, in all the world, will have so many relatives (about him), as he who makes large gift, and does not give way to anger

kurals.tr: Kaakkai Karavaa Karaindhunnum Aakkamum / Annanee Raarkke Ula
kurals.m: The crows do not conceal (their prey), but will call out for others (to share with them) while they eat it; wealth will be with those who show a similar disposition (towards their relatives)

kurals.tr: Podhunokkaan Vendhan Varisaiyaa Nokkin / Adhunokki Vaazhvaar Palar
kurals.m: Many relatives will live near a king, when they observe that he does not look on all alike, but that he looks on each man according to his merit

kurals.tr: Thamaraakik Thatrurandhaar Sutram Amaraamaik / Kaaranam Indri Varum
kurals.m: Those who have been friends and have afterwards forsaken him, will return and join themselves (to him), when the cause of disagreement is not to be found in him

kurals.tr: Uzhaippirindhu Kaaranaththin Vandhaanai Vendhan / Izhaith Thirundhu Ennik Kolal
kurals.m: When one may have left him, and for some cause has returned to him, let the king fulfil the object (for which he has come back) and thoughtfully receive him again
